overview: deConfUSIon is a research fUSI toolbox. Load a dataset, confirm its dimensions and timing, run QC, then apply only the preprocessing needed for the experiment.
load: Supported image arrays are [Y X T] for 2D and [Y X Z T] for 3D or step motor data. The loader keeps the acquired frame count, records tsec when available, and reports the detected animal, scan, dimensions, and TR.
qc: Run Full QC before interpreting maps. Inspect frame outliers, baseline coverage, temporal sampling, and the raw movie. Frame interpolation changes only rejected frames and preserves a 4D array shape.
psc: PSC is 100*(signal-baseline)/baseline. Baseline samples must be finite and positive. SCM rebaseline uses 100*(PSC-newBaseline)/(100+newBaseline), so the displayed trace and exported values use the same definition.
scm: In SCM GUI, edit the baseline start and end times and press Enter or leave the field. The ROI trace and map are recalculated immediately from the selected time window; exported values use that same window.
pcaica: PCA and ICA show the active dataset identity at the top of the window. Processing is chunked to avoid constructing a second full movie in memory. Select components carefully and save a new output before closing.
standardized: Standardized Analysis presets: A Standard A fast, B Standard B slow, C 2D awake, D 2D anesthesized, E 3D awake, F 3D anesthesized, and G motor anesthesized. The preset validates dimensions before running and leaves optional PCA auto removal off until reviewed.
trigger: Trigger Controller: verify the probe and timing units, frame start and active windows, StimBox/PulsePal settings, and motor positions before arming a scan. The live log records moves, saved files, key events, and errors.
fc: Functional connectivity uses finite-sample t statistics and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over unique ROI pairs. Review valid sample counts and q-values before interpreting a network.
registration: Registration aligns the functional image and atlas labels. Confirm orientation, slice order, landmarks, and overlay geometry before saving a transform or extracting regions.
mask: Mask Editor defines include/exclude voxels for maps and ROI traces. Save masks with the dataset identity and check that the mask matches the current slice geometry.
video: Video GUI displays the selected PSC map over the underlay through time. Confirm baseline, signal window, signed color limits, and alpha modulation before exporting.
timecourse: Time-Course Viewer plots ROI traces against seconds. Check the selected baseline and event windows and use the same limits when comparing datasets.
memory: For large data, close unused figures, process one dataset at a time, and use chunked PCA/ICA and QC. The loader selects the image variable instead of loading duplicate large arrays. A 3D dataset can still require several gigabytes for the original image itself.
motion_correction: Motion Correction groups three choices behind one chooser with an explicit START action. Frame rejection marks unusable frames for interpolation and lets you choose the sigma threshold and high/low direction. Despiking suppresses short voxel-wise MAD transients with a robust Z threshold. Scrubbing lets you choose DVARS or global signal, linear or PCHIP interpolation, and optional edge trimming. The raw acquisition remains unchanged; a named derived dataset is added to the dropdown and saved in the background.
chop_data: Chop Data removes a specified number of seconds from the beginning and/or end of a recording. The output keeps the remaining frames, tsec values and TR, records the original frame indices, and receives a name such as 30s_start_30s_end so it can be selected in later modules.
save_queue: Large 3D outputs are written through a cooperative temporary-file queue. Metadata is written first, image chunks are appended to a temporary MAT file, and the finished file is atomically renamed only after validation. A queued or saving label in the dataset list means the source file is still being finalized.
registration_3d: 3D registration first estimates an automatic transform from the functional reference to the underlay or atlas, then allows manual landmark and orientation review. Always inspect the overlay in several slices before committing the transform; the saved registration metadata remains tied to the dataset identity.
atlas_regions: Atlas colors are assigned from the atlas label table and kept consistent between overlays and region summaries. When a coarse analysis is needed, select a parent region grouping (for example cortex or hippocampus) instead of averaging arbitrary small labels; the original labels remain available for detailed analysis.
exports: Exports include the source identity, schema version, tsec when known, baseline window, and processing metadata. Keep generated analysis folders separate from raw data.
troubleshooting: Popups open maximized on the Studio monitor. If a control is clipped, maximize the owning figure. If timing is uncertain, inspect the loader report and tsec before filtering. If a baseline is invalid, choose a window containing finite positive signal rather than accepting an extreme percentage.
about: Help content is shared across the GUIs. The full manual is docs/deConfUSIon_User_Manual_2026-09-06.html; the June 2026 PDF is retained as a legacy reference.
